data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim iff an idealized observer with complete knowledge of the system's reasoning and goals would treat them as interchangeable in all contexts without loss of predictive or explanatory power.", "mechanism": "The system maintains a meta-level model of an ideal observer that can inspect its full belief state and inference traces. When two conclusions appear to agree, the system queries the ideal observer model: 'Are these two conclusions the same proposition given all I know?' If the observer answers yes, they are merged.", "scope": {"covers": ["systems with a meta-cognitive capability", "conclusions that can be compared by an internal observer model"], "excludes": ["systems without self-modeling capacity", "conclusions that are opaque to the system's own introspection"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "The ideal observer judges two conclusions as identical, but after merging, a new fact is added that contradicts the merged conclusion while being consistent with one of the original distinct conclusions.", "eval": "program:observer_merge_contradiction"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion relies on the fidelity of the system's self-model. Eager merging risks overconfidence in the ideal observer's completeness. Reluctant merging risks failing to unify genuinely equivalent claims due to limitations in the observer's reasoning."}
